div.head: NATIONALISTS AND THE WATER.
div.p: THE NATIONALISTS AND THE WATER.
FORD ELECLION,

FORECAST OF THE GENERAL ELECTION. At a meeting of the Irish National Federation on Wed- I nesday at Dublin, Mr. John Dillon' M.P., said the result of the Waterford election had not altered his opinion as to the necessity his party was under to contest that seat. He deeply and sincerely regretted that they had been defeated, but there were only four or five constituen- cies in Ireland in which victory for the Parnellites was possible. Mr. John Redmond, if he succeeded in obtaining even a considerable minority after the next general election, would not be able to hold his followers together. The Parnellite policy was a policy of faction and of personalities, and the result of the Waterford election would not seriously interrupt the march for- ward of the Irish nation.—Mr. Win. O'Brien also ex- pressed the belief that it was their duty to contest Waterford, and said Mr. Davitt's action during the con- test would be one of the most glorious parts of his life. Mr. Redmond got the Tory vote, and his party terrorised the anti-Parnellites from going to the poll. At the general election the anti-Parnellites would win 82 of the 85 Irish constituencies.—Mr. T. D. Sullivan, M.P., also spoke.
ABOLITION OF SECOND-CLASS FARES.

The Cheshire Line 9 Railway Company and the Manchester, Sheffield, and Lincolnshire Railway from Wrexham to Chester and on its other sections abolished second-class tickets yesterday morning. The second-class carriages will be handed over to the third-class passengers, while second-class con- tract ticket-holders will have the privilege of tra- velling first-class until the expiration ot their contracts.

div.head: WARRINGTON TOWN COUNCIL
div.p: WARRINGTON TOWN COUNCIL
A meeting of this Council will be held at the Town Hall, on Tuesday next, when among other matters the following business will be dealt with. THE CABMEN'S SHELTER.—" CABBY" WILL NOT

_ SUBSCRIBE. Mr. A. Woods and Mr. A. Browne have addressed the following letter to the Town Clerk :—" We believe that your Watch Committee have adopted the Act under which they have the power to take over such Shelter. We are entirely unable to make the cabmen subscribe the proper amount for the maintenance of such Shelter, and such Shelter was yesterday closed by the under- signed (Alfred Woods), in order to see if we could not make the men do something, but they have not at- tempted to do anything. There is the sum of £l2 13s. 11d, owing to me the undersigned (Alfred Woods) for money advanced by me to pay gas, water, and ground rent, and there is the sum of /71t, due to me the undersigned (Arthur Browne), for moneys overpaid by me on the Cabmen's Shelter Account. We would,there- fore, suggest that you should put this letter before the Watch Committee this afternoon. and see if they cannot arrange to take over the Shelter, and pay off the exist- ing debt M £l3 10s. 11d."—On the matter being laid be- fore the Watch Committee, they decided to take over the Cabmen's Shelter on the terms of theabove letter. AN INSANITARY AREA. The Sanitary Committee report that the Medical Officer of Health having called the attention of the Committee to the necessity of an Improvement Scheme under the Housing of the Working Classes Act, 1690, for the re-arrangement and re-construction of the streets and houses within a certain area defined by him in and near Dial-street, and he haying represented that the sanitary defects in such area cannot be effectually remedied otherwise:than by an Improvement Scheme, the Committee have resolved that a report be prepared showing the houses, courts, and alleys that are—(l). Fit for human habitation :: (a') unfit, but capable of being made fit for human habitation; (3) unfit and incapable of being made fit for human habita- tion; and also showing in what manner it is proposed to improve the said area so aS to remedy the sanitary defects in such area. It was also resolved that the Medical Officer of Health and the Borough Surveyor be instructed to prepare such report, and that they be authorized to obtain such assistance as they may require for such purpose ; and that the Medical officer of Health prepare an analysis of the death-rate during the last five years, showing the ages and causes of mortality, in the said area. THE CORPORA-TIM AND THE SCHOOL OF ART. The Museum, Sze., Committee again recommend the transfer of the Sehool of Art to the Corporation,. The conditions of the transfer as laid down in a letter of Mr. W. Owen, the hon. sec. oi the School of Art, are the following :—First That the Corporation shall peg for the casts and other property in the School Building which have been given by private donors, such a sum as will cover all liabilities of the present Trustees and COmmittee, not exceeding £200.--Second : That the Corporation shall take over the School exactly on the same covenants as is now held by the Trustees under the Trust Deed, and that the Corporation shall indemnify the Trustees from all liability under such Trust Deed, and also under the Deed of Conveyance of the property from Lord Win- marleigh, dated 37st December, 1677 (referred to, in the Trust Deed), and also against any claim which the Lords of the Treasury may have for repayment of the grant made by them to the &hoot.— Third : That the Corporation shall undertake to carry on the school as an efficient School of Art.—Furth : That the Corperation shall take over the engaeements of the Council with the present teaching staff.—Fifth : That the transfer of the school to the Corporation shall take place as and from the Ist January, 1892:—Sixth : That the Corporation pay all expenses in relation to the transfer. TECHNICAL EDUCATION. The General Purposes Committee.will recommend that the sum of seventy pounds out of the Borough Fund be voted to the Maiseurn,Library, Arts, and Techoical In- struction Corm-nate& for the purchase of appliances for Technical Instruction, and to enable the Committee to earn a like grant from the Science and Art Department. PROPOSED ^ PURCHASE OF TFI3MILITIA IittIRRACKS. The Mayor, Alderman Platt, and Ceuncillor litlackhurst having been authorised to wait upon the Finance Commit- tee of the County Council with regard to the purchase of the old militia Barracks in Wilson Pattea-etreet, the Mayor and Councillor Blackhtust report to the General Purposes Cemmittee as follows. We be to report the result of the interview which the deputation, appointed by your Chrnmittee, had with the County Council of Lancashire on the subject of the purchase- of the Militia Storehouee at Warrington. We waited upon the Finance Committee of the County or, the 16th December inst.,and after laying our views befoe them were, informed that the price at which they ware prepareOto sell the pre- mises to the Corporation is. £4,750. -- ST. PAUL'S CHURCH BELL RINGERS, WARRINGTON. INTERESTING PRESENTATION.. The annual supper in connection with the above took place at the Mason's Arms, Mill-st., on Mon- day evening. A tibstantial repast was provided, and was done full jiistice to. After the tables had been cleared, Mr. O. Bebbington, jun., was voted to the chair. The usual loyal toasts were given. Mr.J. Seed then rose to propose the toast of "Our officers," viz., the secretary (Mr. T. M. Moore) find treasurer (Mr. G. Bebbington, jun.). In a brief speech he al- luded to the satisfactory manner in which,the busi- ness had been conducted during their tenure of office, and expressed a hope that they would serve them for many years to come. The secretary res- ponded, and thanked them heartily for the manner in which the toast had been received, and assured them that nothing should be wanting on his part to further the interests of ringing and ringers. Ile now had a pleasant duty to perform, which was to pre- sent to his co-adjutor in office a handsome album as a token of esteem from his brother-ringers. In making the presentation,he (the sec.) alluded to the kindness and courteous manner shown at all times by the conductor. He then read the following in- scription :—"Presented to Mr.G.Bebbington.jun.,con- ductor, as a mark ol• esteem from his fellow-ringers. T. IL Moore, M. Hosker, J. Seed, J.R. Hill, A.Oxley, F. Stout, J. M. Moore, Levi Jones." In 'acknow- ledging the presentation, the conductor begged to thank one and all for the kind presentation of such a handsome albunt4.,and assured thercwit would be the greatest pleasure for him to look:upon it with pride and satisfaction,not for the valusa of the same, but as a token of the respect and kind feeling which it carried with it. He could only say.in conclusion, that so long as his services were of any use to them it would be the greatest pleasure for him to be at, their disposal to further the art of campanology. The rest of the evening was spent in a very convi- vial manner, songs being given by several members - The singing of the-National Anthem terminated a very enjoyable evening,

RE WILLIAM OWEN DECEASED.—Pursuant to the statute 22nd and 23rd vie. ca,p. 35, notice is hereby given that all creditors and other persons having any claims against the estate of William Owen,late of Canal Farm, Haydock, in the County of Lancaster, farmer, deceased (who died on the 2nd day of July, 1891, and whose will was proved in the District Registry at Liverpool, of her Majesty's High Court of Justice, on the 14th day of August. 1891) are hereby required to Bend the particulars of their claims to us the under- signed, the solicitors for the executors, on or before the 13th day of February, 1892, after which date the executors will proceed to distribute the assets of the said deceased amongst the persons entitled thereto, having regard only to the claims and demands of which they shall then have had notice. Dated this Ist day of January, 1892. JENKINS AND UNSWORTH. Bank Chambers, No. 1, Winwick-st., Warrington. Solicitors for the executors.

COUNTY OF CHESTER, TO WIT. NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN, that the next GENERAL QUARTER SESSIONS of the Peace for the COUNTY OF CHESTER will be holden at the CASTLE OF CHESTER, in and for the said County, on MONDAY, the 4th day of January next, at Half-past Eleven o'clock in the Forenoon, when the Grand Jury will be empannelled. The hearing of all Appeals arising within the Hun- dreds of Broxton, Eddisbury, Nantwich and Wirral, forming the Chester District, and the trials of all pri- soners committed from such Hundreds, will take place at such Sessions. The Grand and Petty Jury for the Chester District must be in attendance at the Castle of Chester, at the opening of the Court on MONDAY, the 4th day of January next, at Half .past Eleven o'clock in the Forenoon. The Court will be Adjourned to the Court House, Nether Knutsford, on WEDNESDAY, the 6th day of Janu- ary next, at Eleven o'clock in the Forenoon. The hear- ing of all Appeals arising within the Hundreds of Bucklow' Macclesfield, and Northwich, forming the Knutsford District, and the trials of all prisoners com- mitted from the last-mentioned Hundreds will take place at such Adjourned Sessions. The Grand and Petty Jury for the Knutsford District must be in attendance at the Court House, Knutsford, at Ow opening of the Court on WEDNESDAY, the 6th day of January next, at Eleven o'clock in the Forenoon. REGINALD POTTS, Clerk of the Peace for the County of Chester. Chester, 15th December, 1891.

TRAGEDY IN LIMERICK. At Limerick, on Saturday, John Carey, 25, labourer, was committed charged with causing the death of his child. The prisoner quarrelled with his wife on Christ- mas Eve, both being intoxicated at the time, and in struggling the child was killed. At the inquest the doc- tor swore the child's death was the result of violence,and the jury returned a verdict accordingly. OUTBREAK OF INFLUENZA. Since the disappearance of the frosty weather the in- fluenza epidemic in Canterbury has spread with alarm- in.' rapidity. Previously the decease was very prevalent, but now almost every family is more or less affected. In ' some cases whole families are prostrated. Some busi- ness houses have had to get assistants from London to take the places of the sufferers. • PRINCE GEORGE'S RECOVERY. Prince George of Wales was able on Wednesday to ac- company his father and mother and the Duke of Clarence and Avondale and the Princesses Victoria and Maud to Sandringham. The special train arrived at Wolferton at four o'clock. Prince George walked unassisted from the station to the carriage which conveyed him to Sand- ringham House.

DEATH OF THE PRINCE OE HOHENLOHE. Prince Victor of Hohenlohe died at half-past four on Thursday morning, at • St. James's Palace. Prince Victor, who died from throat affection, was visited dur- ing his illness by both the Queen and the Prince of Wales. He was a retired admiral of the British fleet, and was also governor and constable of Windsor Castle. The deceased Prince was born at Lagenburg, and was half-nephew of Queen Victoria. He was, perhaps, bet- ter known by his second title of Count Gleichen.

MORE BORROWING. The General Purposes Committee recommend that the Town Clerk be instructed to apply to the Local Government Board for permission to borrow the said sum of £4,750, for the purchase of the old barracks, and also the sum of £4,100 for the purchase of the premises at Market Gate, and the sum of £4,500 for the purchase of the premises at Bridge Foot which have recently been acquired by the Corporation. WHAT DOES IT MEAN? Councillor HILL gives notice that he will move the following resolaion :—" That all tenders for work; or estimates, or contracts for the satne,be sent in envelopes supplied by the firm or person who send the estimates or contracts, and not in those supplied by the Corpora- tion, and be opened by the Chairman of Om Committee to whom it is addressed." THE WATER RATE. The Water Committee have resolved that, in order to make the Water works Accounts correspond in date with the other accounts of the Corporation the next water rate be levied for the nine months ending the 29th of September, 1892, and that an additional month be allowed to owners of cottage property for the payment of composition in respect of such water rate. After the 29th September, 1892, the water rates will be collected half-yearly, on the 25th March and 29th September, in each year.

YESTERDAY'S FOOTBALL. Bolton Wanderers beat Derby county ; North End beat Darwen. A SCHOONER AND SIX LIVES LOST. The Canarvan schooner Catherine Richards, with six hands, was lost on Thursday in Ballyheigue Bay, County Kerry. PEACE PROSPECTS ON THE CONTINENT. ROME, rRIDAY.—King Humbert held the usual New Year reception of the members of both chambers of Parliament to-day, and, during a short speech, he declared that never had a year commenced with better prospects of the maintenance of peace. 85,000 COLLIERS IDLE. Yesterday work was entirely suspended in the collieries throughout South Wales and Monmouthshire, at least 85,000 men being idle. The deadlock pending negotia- tions causes great anxiety, and intense excitement pre- vails in all the colliery districts. THE DUBLIN CASTLE EXPLOSION. OFFICIAL INSPEC HON. Major Majendie, Chief Inspector of Explosives, has arrived. No fresh facts have been elicited up to the present, and the police have no clue which would en- able them to trace the means by which the explosion was brought about. THE DUKE OF DEVONSHIRE'S FAREWELL ADDRESS. Ihe Duke of Devonshire's valedictory address to the electors of Rossendale was issued yesterday. After thanking the electors for continuing their confidence in him when he considered it his duty to protest against the abandonment of the pledges of his former colleagues his lordship says the country had been saved from violent constitutional change, and the more closely the policy they had resisted was examined the less approval would it receive. THE CHARGE AGAINST MR. HASTINGS, M.P. Mr. George Woodyatt Hastings, member of Parliament for East Worcestershire, was charged on remand at Bow- street, yesterday, with having defrauded persons for whom he voas a trustee under the will of Major John Brown, deceased, of £15,000, invested in mortgages in Worcestershire. The accused seemed greatly dejected, and stepped into the dock with evident effort. Mr. Avory, for the prosecution, stated how the trust funds were invested, and proceeded to read extracts from a diary found upon the accused. Evidence of the defen- dant's financial transactions as chairman of the Pilstall Coal and Iron Company was taken, and the accused was remanded till Friday next.
